results.title: Aggregation - Federated Learning Platform
results.content: This guide provides an overview of the available model aggregation strategies in our federated machine learning platform. Federated learning is a machine learning approach where a model is trained across multiple decentralized devices (clients) holding local data samples, without exchanging them. In federated learning, model aggregation is a crucial step, because models trained on local client data need to be combined (aggregated) in order to produce a more robust and reliable global model. * **Model Drift**: As a result of data heterogeneity, when local models are trained independently on disparate datasets, they may diverge significantly from the global model. * **Impact on Global Model**: The aggregated global model might not capture the true underlying pattern of the entire dataset, particularly when the data distribution extremely heterogenous across clients. These scenarios emphasize the need for efficient, secure, and adaptable model aggregation methods in federated learning systems, particularly in environments where data privacy and minimal data transmission are crucial. 1. Each client trains the model on their local data. * FedProx improves FedAvg by dealing with data heterogeneity and challenges like varying computation and communication capabilities of the clients. * Similar to FedAvg in aggregating model parameter updates, i.e., the code executed at the central server as well as the communication steps between server and clients are the same as for FedAvg. This prevents large model drifts due to client data heterogeneity, which otherwise might infect the global model and thus the whole system. It involves circulating models among clients for training before aggregation. * The training steps are similar to FedAvg as described above, except that, at selected times, the models are circulated among the clients instead of being sent to the central server. After the circulation step, the models are continued to be trained at their new clients, such that the circulated model effectively "sees" more data than available at its original client. * After aggregation, the global model is returned to the clients, which continue their local training until another circulation or aggregation round begins. * Benchmarks: For strong data imbalance among clients, FedDC still achieves around 63% test accuracy (whereas FedAvg/FedProx achieve ~50% in such cases).
